memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But the king of Egypt said, "Moses and Aaron, why are you taking the people away from their labour? Get back to your work!" Then Pharaoh said, "Look, the people of the land are now numerous, and you are stopping them from working."" - Exodus 5:4-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Pharaoh's response is instructive. He does not debate whether God exists. He simply reframes worship as a productivity problem. Get back to work.

That is how a slave-driving system always thinks. People are valued for output. Anything that does not produce is a waste — including worship, rest, and time with God.

We should recognise this voice, because it speaks in our world too. It tells us we cannot afford a Sabbath, that prayer is time we do not have, that stopping is indulgence. Many believers live under a Pharaoh made of deadlines and expectations.

God thought differently. He built rest into creation itself and later wrote it into the commandments — and He grounded Israel's Sabbath in the memory that they had once been slaves. Rest is a declaration that we are not slaves any more.

Jesus said it plainly: come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest (Mt 11:28). His yoke is not another form of Egypt.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What voice in my life tells me that time with God is time wasted?
2. When did I last genuinely rest and worship without guilt?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, free me from the Pharaoh of endless demands. Teach me to rest in You without feeling I must earn my worth. Amen.
